cases.question: How should the incident be classified at the cutoff?

events.text: Decision rule in force: classify capacity only if CPU is above 80%; classify network only if packet loss is above 5%; otherwise classify transient.
Observed: API latency is high, CPU is 42%, and packet-loss monitoring reports 1%.
The incident is escalated for deeper network inspection.
A monitoring bug is discovered. Packet loss during sequence 2 was actually 12%, although this was not known at sequence 2.

cases.question: What procurement decision was justified at the cutoff?

events.text: Procurement rule in force: approve when SLA is at least 99.9% and certification is valid, unless a sanctions match is known. Reject if a sanctions match is known.
Vendor SLA is 99.95%, certification is valid, and the sanctions check returns no match.
Contract drafting begins.
The sanctions provider backfills a missed record: the vendor was on the sanctions list before sequence 2, but this fact was not available to procurement then.

cases.question: What transaction action was justified at the cutoff?

events.text: Fraud rule in force: block if an account-takeover signal is known; challenge if either device or location is unfamiliar; otherwise allow.
The device is familiar, location is familiar, and no account-takeover signal is present.
The payment settles.
Support later confirms the account had been taken over before sequence 2; the takeover signal was generated late and was unavailable at the cutoff.

cases.question: Under the rule in force at the cutoff, should the release ship?

events.text: Release rule v1: ship if all required tests pass and there is no severity-1 incident.
All required tests pass and there is no severity-1 incident.
Security leadership issues rule v2: any unresolved severity-2 security finding now requires a hold.
The release has an unresolved severity-2 security finding.

cases.question: What credit decision was justified at the cutoff?

events.text: Credit rule in force: approve if leverage is at most 3.0x and there is no known covenant breach; otherwise decline.
Reported leverage is 2.7x and no covenant breach is known.
The facility is approved subject to documentation.
Audited numbers later restate leverage at sequence 2 to 3.4x. The restatement was not knowable at the cutoff.

cases.question: Which route was justified at the cutoff?

events.text: Routing rule: choose route A if its known travel time is under 40 minutes and no closure is known; otherwise choose route B.
Route A is estimated at 32 minutes and no closure is known. Route B is estimated at 45 minutes.
The vehicle departs on route A.
A road authority feed arrives late showing route A had been closed shortly before sequence 2; the closure was not in the system at the cutoff.

cases.question: What scaling action was justified at the cutoff?

events.text: Capacity rule: scale if the known next-hour demand forecast exceeds 80 units; otherwise do not scale.
The available next-hour forecast is 68 units.
No scaling action is taken.
A corrected model run later shows that demand at sequence 2 should have been forecast at 91 units; the correction did not exist at the cutoff.

cases.question: Under the policy and facts known at the cutoff, should access be granted?

events.text: Access policy v3: grant if employment is active and the requested project is assigned. No geography restriction exists in v3.
Employment is active and the requested project is assigned.
Policy v4 is adopted, adding a geography restriction for this data class.
The requester's geography would violate the new v4 restriction.
